summary: Registering an app for Google Business Profile APIs requires creating a Google Cloud project, configuring OAuth credentials, and submitting an access application form to request quota. The main catch is that access is gated by a manual review process; project quota is locked at 0 Requests Per Minute (QPM) until Google approves the application, which typically takes 2 to 4+ weeks.

difficulty.headline: API access is gated by a mandatory manual application process, and API requests remain completely blocked at 0 QPM quota until Google grants approval.

factors.label: Zero Quota Lock
factors.detail: Enabling Business Profile APIs leaves your project with a 0 QPM quota limit, preventing any testing or live API calls until manual approval.

evidence.quote: A quota of 0 QPM means the project has not yet been approved, while 300 QPM indicates that access has been approved.

factors.label: Extended Review Wait
factors.detail: Standard review times are quoted at 14 days, but high application volume frequently pushes waiting periods past 3 to 4 weeks.

evidence.quote: Google states that Business Profile API access requests are normally reviewed within 14 days.

factors.label: Account Eligibility Requirement
factors.detail: Applicants must maintain a verified Google Business Profile active for at least 60 days before applying for direct API access.

evidence.quote: Manage a Google Business Profile that has been verified and active for at least 60 days.

can_test_before_approval.detail: Google Cloud projects configured with the Business Profile APIs default to 0 Requests Per Minute (0 QPM), blocking all API execution until the access application is explicitly approved by Google.

evidence.quote: A quota of 0 QPM means the project has not yet been approved, while 300 QPM indicates that access has been approved.

requirements.label: Google Cloud Project
requirements.detail: A Google Cloud Console project with Business Profile APIs enabled.

evidence.quote: Before using the API, you must configure your Google Cloud project, enable the Business Profile APIs, and set up OAuth credentials and the consent screen.

requirements.label: Verified Business Profile (60+ Days)
requirements.detail: An active Google Business Profile managed by the applying entity for at least 60 days.

evidence.quote: Manage a Google Business Profile that has been verified and active for at least 60 days.

requirements.label: OAuth Consent Screen Metadata
requirements.detail: Configured application name, logo, homepage, privacy policy link, and terms of service link.

evidence.quote: From there, you can update the application name and the logo, as well as include a link to your terms of service and privacy policy.

requirements.label: API Access Application Form
requirements.detail: Submission of the official Google Business Profile API access and quota increase request form.

steps.title: Configure Google Cloud Project and Enable APIs
steps.detail: Create or select a Google Cloud Project and enable the required Business Profile API services (such as My Business Account Management API and Business Profile Performance API).
steps.agent_assist: Generate list of required Google Business Profile API service names and setup commands for Google Cloud Console.

evidence.quote: Before using the API, you must configure your Google Cloud project, enable the Business Profile APIs, and set up OAuth credentials and the consent screen.

steps.title: Configure OAuth Consent Screen and OAuth Client Credentials
steps.detail: In Google Cloud Console, configure the consent screen with application metadata and create an OAuth Client ID credential set.
steps.agent_assist: Draft app name, description, privacy policy text outline, terms of service link format, authorized domain list, and requested scope list (https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage).

evidence.quote: From there, you can update the application name and the logo, as well as include a link to your terms of service and privacy policy.

steps.title: Verify Account Eligibility Requirements
steps.detail: Ensure the applicant Google Account has managed a verified Google Business Profile active for at least 60 days and uses an email on a business domain.
steps.agent_assist: Compile pre-application checklist verifying account age, profile verification status, domain email alignment, and required documentation.

evidence.quote: Manage a Google Business Profile that has been verified and active for at least 60 days.

steps.title: Submit Google Business Profile API Access Request Form
steps.detail: Fill out and submit Google's official access request form with your project ID, business use case details, target locations, and technical architecture.
steps.agent_assist: Draft clear use-case explanations, workflow architecture summaries, user consent mechanisms, and data protection descriptions to paste into the request form.

steps.title: Wait for Google Security Review and Quota Provisioning
steps.detail: Google reviews your access application. Reviews normally take 14 days but can take longer during high application volume. Do not submit duplicate applications while pending.

evidence.quote: Google states that Business Profile API access requests are normally reviewed within 14 days.

steps.title: Provide Demo Account Upon Request
steps.detail: If requested by Google during review, provide a functioning live demo account of your application within 7 days to verify compliance with Google policies.
steps.agent_assist: Draft step-by-step demo instructions and test user walkthrough documentation for Google's reviewers.

evidence.quote: Upon request from Google, you must provide a demo account to your API tool within seven days of the request.

steps.title: Verify Quota Provisioning and Enable Production Integration
steps.detail: Check your Google Cloud Console quota metrics to confirm the Business Profile API quota has increased from 0 QPM to 300 QPM.
steps.agent_assist: Provide validation script to test API authorization tokens once quota reaches 300 QPM.

evidence.quote: A quota of 0 QPM means the project has not yet been approved, while 300 QPM indicates that access has been approved.

gotchas.title: Submitting Duplicate Applications Delays Approval
gotchas.detail: Submitting multiple access or quota request forms while an initial request is pending can reset your queue position or create conflicting support files.

evidence.quote: Please note: Do not submit additional applications while your initial application is pending.

gotchas.title: Failure to Provide Demo Account Causes Rejection
gotchas.detail: Google may request a live demo account during policy review. Failing to provide working credentials within 7 days constitutes a policy violation.

evidence.quote: Upon request from Google, you must provide a demo account to your API tool within seven days of the request.

gotchas.title: Indirect Third-Party API Access Prohibited
gotchas.detail: You cannot build wrapper APIs or share project credentials that allow end-clients or agencies to access Business Profile APIs programmatically without their own approved Cloud projects.

evidence.quote: You cannot provide indirect access to your Business Profile project.

blockers.problem: API Requests Fail with Quota Exceeded / Zero Quota Error
blockers.why: The Google Cloud Project has enabled the APIs but Google has not yet approved the access application, keeping quota locked at 0 QPM.
blockers.fix: Check project quota in Google Cloud Console. If it reads 0 QPM, your access request is still pending approval. Once approved, quota will show 300 QPM.

evidence.quote: A quota of 0 QPM means the project has not yet been approved, while 300 QPM indicates that access has been approved.

blockers.problem: Application Status Stuck in 'In Progress' Past 14 Days
blockers.why: Unusually high application volume at Google can extend review times past the standard 14-day window.
blockers.fix: Do not submit duplicate access applications. Retain your original Case ID, monitor Cloud Console for 300 QPM, and post follow-ups in the official community with '[API]' in the title.

evidence.quote: Please note: Do not submit additional applications while your initial application is pending.

blockers.problem: Google Project Deactivated Due to Policy Non-Compliance
blockers.why: Failure to follow third-party policies, failure to respond to demo account requests, or unauthorized programmatic modifications.
blockers.fix: Correct the non-compliant policies or user access patterns in your software, then reapply using Google's official reapplication form.

uncertain: Exact response timeframes when API access reviews exceed the standard 14-day evaluation window.
